sandbox.details: What each tier protects and costs
sandbox.measured: Measured on this computer on 2026-11-22 with npm ci, a TypeScript build and a test run of a small project.
sandbox.off: Off — the agent works with your rights, as today. No cost.
sandbox.native: Agent's own sandbox — Claude Code and Codex hold their commands to the project folder with the system's own isolation; their commands' network is off, through the agent's exit, or open, while the agent itself still calls its model. Almost no cost. Claude Code on Windows needs `claude sandbox install` once; Codex on Windows needs its Windows sandbox set up.
sandbox.container: Container — the agent itself runs in a Docker or Podman container that sees only the project, with none of your sign-ins; its only way out is a small proxy beside it, which lets through its model's addresses only, everything through the agent's exit, or anything. Starts in about {{start}} s and Docker holds about {{memory}} MB. A project on a Windows drive builds {{build}}× slower ({{native}} s → {{container}} s) and searches {{search}}× slower; one inside WSL's own disk runs at full speed ({{wsl}} s).
sandbox.notProtected: What a sandbox does not protect: the project itself can still be changed or deleted; Claude Code's and Codex's own file and web tools are held by the permission requests rather than by the sandbox, and their model calls go out as before; MCP servers and hooks run outside it; an API key the agent gets is visible to it, and its model service sees what it sends.

enabled.description: Copies Kettu’s sessions, settings, memory, artifacts and attachments into one file a day. A day missed while the computer was off is made up once, the next time Kettu runs.

time.name: Time

problem.migrating: Kettu is moving its data to a new format; the backup waits until it is done.
problem.failed: The last backup did not finish.

restore.name: Restore from backup
restore.description: Puts a backup’s data in place of Kettu’s, after saving the data it replaces as a backup of its own.
restore.keywords: backup restore recover roll back import
restore.title: Restore this backup?
restore.replaces: It replaces Kettu’s sessions, settings, memory, artifacts and attachments. What came after the backup goes, but a copy of the data now is saved in the backup folder first.
restore.keeps: Paired devices, the Kettu account sign-in, Marketplace keys and proxy subscriptions are never in backups, and stay as they are.
restore.restart: Running agents stop, and Kettu restarts to restore.
restore.restoring: Kettu restarts to restore the backup…
restore.safety: The data it replaced is in {{safety}}, in the backup folder.

backup.note: Left out: this computer’s keys and pairings, the Kettu account sign-in, Marketplace keys and proxy subscriptions, which hold secrets; and caches, logs and the search index, which Kettu rebuilds.

notes.scope: A project may have a roster of its own; the others use this one.
notes.manager: What new manager sessions start with. A manager only reads and dispatches, so a cheap model does.
notes.roster: The manager dispatches to workers by name. A persona goes only into that worker session's first message, never into the agent's own files. ★ marks the default reviewer.
notes.limits: A task starts when you write to the manager; past a limit Kite has the manager stop and ask you.

scope.name: Settings for
scope.description: The roster for every project, or one project’s own.

project.name: Own settings for this project
project.description: On, this project's manager sessions use the roster and choices below; off, they use the ones for all projects.

suggestion.name: Suggested manager
suggestion.description: The agent, profile and model new manager sessions start with.
suggestion.none: No suggestion: keep the current choice

empty.title: No workers yet
empty.hint: Start from a roster suggested by the agents on this computer, then change it as you like.

autoReview.name: Automatic review
autoReview.description: When code is finished, Kite hands it to the default reviewer and back until it is approved or the rounds run out. The default for new manager sessions.
autoReview.noReviewer: The roster has no default reviewer yet, so automatic review does nothing.

rounds.name: Review rounds
rounds.description: Not approved by then, the manager stops and asks you.

approvals.name: Workers' permission requests
approvals.description: The default for new manager sessions, which each can change. The project's own auto-approve level always applies first.

concurrent.name: Workers at once
concurrent.description: More dispatches wait for a worker to finish. Only one code-writing worker works in a folder at a time.

turns.name: Per task, at most
turns.description: Once the worker turns are spent, the manager dispatches no more and asks you.

budget.name: Token budget
budget.description: Tokens the manager and its workers may use per task; models Kite has prices for also show a cost.

afterRestart.name: After Kite restarts
afterRestart.description: What workers a restart cut do: go on one at a time, within the workers-at-once limit, or only tell the manager.

worker.lead: The manager dispatches by name; review and planning workers only read.
worker.name: Name
worker.readOnly: This role only reads: Kite keeps it from changing files; reading and read-only commands work.
worker.worktree: A new worktree for each dispatch
worker.worktreeHint: It can work beside other code-writing workers; its changes stay on a new branch, which Kite never merges itself.
worker.sandboxHint: When the manager runs in a sandbox, its workers run in the manager's.
worker.container: A worker in a container gets none of Kite's tools, so it cannot report with report_work. Kite takes its last reply as its report instead, and a review's verdict from the VERDICT line in it.
worker.personaPlaceholder: Such as: You write clean code with small changes, and read before you change.
worker.personaNote: Goes only into this worker session's first message, never into the agent's own settings.
worker.repeated: The roster already has this name.

writer.name: Writer
writer.persona: You write clean code with small changes, read before you change, and run the tests that matter.

reviewer.name: Reviewer
reviewer.persona: You are a strict but practical reviewer: read git diff, check correctness, edge cases, tests and project conventions. Give changes only for what must change; note small things as nit and still approve.

planner.name: Planner
planner.persona: You research and plan: read code and docs, give steps that can be acted on and the risks, and change no files.

helper.name: Helper
helper.persona: You do small, clear jobs: tests, renames, docs, formatting, as the task says, without improvising.

features.keywords: features switches turn off hide lighter bloat load
features.note: Sessions, the terminal, the browser, Git, artifacts and the Marketplace are Kite's core and always on. A feature turned off no longer loads or runs, and turns back on any time without a restart; code it already loaded leaves memory at the next launch.
features.sandboxHeld: Turns off only while the default sandbox is Off, since new sessions still start in it. Set it to Off in Agents › Sandbox first.

computerUse.name: Computer use
computerUse.description: Agents operate apps on this computer. It has its own switch on the Computer use page.

computerElevated.name: Programs run as administrator
computerElevated.description: Part of computer use, chosen on its page.

board.name: Task board
board.description: Sort sessions into To do, In progress, Review and Done on the Overview; agents move theirs to Review when done.

manager.name: Manager mode
manager.description: One session splits the task among worker agents and checks their reports.

bestOfN.name: Best of N
bestOfN.description: Send one message to 2 to 4 agents or models at once, each in its own worktree, and keep the best.

routines.name: Routines
routines.description: Start sessions on a schedule or on GitHub events. Off, nothing runs on schedule.

github.name: GitHub automation
github.description: The issue inbox, merge when checks pass, PR watch and routines' GitHub triggers. Off, Kite reads nothing from GitHub.

sandbox.name: Sandbox
sandbox.description: Run sessions in the agent's own sandbox or in a container.

devices.name: Mobile devices
devices.description: Agents run and check apps on iOS simulators, Android emulators and connected phones. Off, Kite stops looking for devices.

secrets.name: Secret cards
secrets.description: Agents ask you for an API key, token or password in a private card, never in the chat.

fileCheckpoints.name: File checkpoints for rewinds
fileCheckpoints.description: Kite keeps a copy of the session's files as each message goes, so going back to a message can restore them too.

agentTheme.name: Agent theme changes
agentTheme.description: Agents read and change Kite's theme colors when you ask them to.

agentNotify.name: Agent notifications
agentNotify.description: Agents send you a desktop notification and a phone push when you asked to be told, or when long work finishes. Your notification settings and muted sessions still apply.

chatBridge.name: Chat apps
chatBridge.description: Drive agents from a Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, QQ or Telegram bot. Off, every bot disconnects.

portForwarding.name: Port forwarding
portForwarding.description: Forward dev server ports of your other computers to this one and open them in the session's browser.

devPreview.name: Dev servers on the phone
devPreview.description: Preview this computer's dev servers on a paired phone.

pickElement.name: Pick elements
pickElement.description: Pick elements of a page in the side browser and comment on them for the agent.

agentSync.name: Agent sync
agentSync.description: The Marketplace's Sync tab: sync MCP servers, skills and instructions across your agents.

webReader.name: Background web reading (Moli)
webReader.description: When an agent’s own fetch cannot read a page that needs JavaScript, it reads the page in the background with Moli, a headless browser. Turning it on downloads Moli (about 42 MB) from GitHub.

sessionTidy.name: Snooze and settle
sessionTidy.description: Snooze a session until later; it comes back then, or sooner if it needs you. Idle sessions and ones whose pull request merged settle out of the list by themselves.

sessionMentions.name: Mention a session
sessionMentions.description: Type @ in the composer, or drag a session's row onto it, to point the agent at another session; it reads that session's history only when it needs to.

zenView.name: Concise thread
zenView.description: Hide tool calls that went well, or show only your messages and the agent's final replies, for each session or by default. Requests and questions always show.
